title.narrative: DRI (Disinformation Resilience in Israel)

description.narrative: Contract related to: DRI (Disinformation Resilience in Israel) - This 18-months crisis response measure has the overarching goal of supporting efforts that alleviate the suffering of the most affected communities and assist in promoting lasting peace. Its first component seeks to assess the damage to health infrastructure and to protect civilians by providing life-saving support to essential health services as well as early warning and disease prevention activities. This component will also help address the vast needs in regard to mental health and psychosocial support for affected communities in Israel and Palestine. The second component aims to assist advocacy efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict. It will also focus on countering disinformation, supporting fact checking to facilitate that public debate is based on reliable information and thereby contribute to an informed and constructive dialogue in support of a lasting peace. A third component will focus on humanitarian mine action, particularly on Digital Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (DEORE) messaging campaigns using social media platforms, and when the situation allows for it, establish explosive ordnance survey and clearance capacity, in particular around critical infrastructure, to facilitate safe movement and delivery of humanitarian aid. The fourth component will focus on the West Bank, focusing on preventing conflict-related violence, ensuring physical safety and well-being, and provide legal services. The focus will be on equipping communities and individuals with skills and support to prevent violence and protect against human rights violations.

title.narrative: Output 1/Activity Package 1: Increased capacity of civil society organizations and media outlets to effectively tackle disinformation and misinformation on social media platforms and communication channels

description.narrative: Activity package 1: Capacity building of civil society organizations and media outlets.1.1 Conduct Stakeholder Mapping and Needs Assessment of Israeli media ecosystem, including media organizations, fact checkers, academics, tech companies and NGOs to analyze capacity gaps and priorities for tackling disinformation in Israel and available strategies and interventions. 1.2 Training Programs for 100 Journalists, media outlets and Civil Society Media Activists. This includes lectures and workshops in newsrooms, delivered by international experts in factchecking and digital investigations, and comprehensive training courses (68 meetings) for local journalists and media activists, tailored development programs (34 sessions each) for news room teams of at least 3 media outlets, and 3 workshops for civil society professionals, including educational intercourse and knowledge exchange with leading fact checkers. 1.3 Development and Dissemination of Practical Guides and Resources for Digital Media Activists, Bloggers and Independent Journalism: Create a centralized online repository as well as 34 digital guides with practical howto manuals, toolkits and tips on topics like performing fact checks, identifying manipulated photos/videos, responsible journalism ethics, and disinformation response. 1.4 Grants and Professional Support for at least two FactChecking or Digital Investigation Activities within Israeli Civil Society. 1.5 Professional Conference for Journalists: serving as an effective platform for sharing the knowledge and insights that surface through the action and connecting Israeli journalists and media outlets to global journalism initiatives (such as the International Fact Checking Network), for advancing a more informed professional discourse around the risks and threats of misinformation and disinformation, as well as best practices, strategies, and methodologies to effectively address them.
